about.title: Morro Bay Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Morro Bay draws heavy foot traffic to its waterfront shops, harbor walkways, and small-town sidewalks along Main Street, and that traffic means uneven pavement, wet tile, and poorly lit stairwells sometimes go unaddressed. If you slipped or tripped at a business, rental property, or public space in San Luis Obispo County, the property owner or manager may bear responsibility if they knew about the hazard, or reasonably should have, and didn't fix it or warn visitors. Proving that knowledge is often the hardest part of a premises liability case, which is why photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage matter so much in the days right after a fall. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened and explain your options. There's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to act. An attorney can help gather the evidence that establishes this before it disappears.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many Morro Bay businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Your Deadline Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: California generally gives you two years to file a premises liability claim, but that window shrinks significantly if a government-owned property or walkway was involved. Pure comparative fault also means partial responsibility on your part doesn't automatically bar recovery, so it's worth having a professional review the facts.

items.question: I fell on a wet floor near the Embarcadero and no one saw it happen. Can I still file a claim?
items.answer: Yes, though it helps your case to have any evidence you can gather, like photos of the wet area, your shoes, or nearby warning signs (or lack of them). An attorney can also request the business's surveillance footage and incident reports, which often capture more than witnesses do. Acting quickly matters since footage can be deleted within days.

items.question: What if the sidewalk or trail I fell on was owned by the City of Morro Bay?
items.answer: Claims against a public entity in California come with a much shorter filing deadline, often just six months, so it's important to act fast. An independent attorney can help determine ownership and file the required government claim before that window closes.

items.question: Does it matter if I was distracted or partly at fault when I fell?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you share some blame, though your compensation may be reduced proportionally. An attorney can help evaluate how fault might be allocated based on the specific hazard and circumstances of your fall.
